title: Read the samples and the waits

blocks.content: To read how the query behaves over time, complete the following steps. If a tab is empty, skip it and go on.

blocks.title: Read the samples and the waits

blocks.content:
Open the **Query samples** tab.

If the tab is empty, skip the next step.

blocks.reftarget: section[data-testid='data-testid Panel header Select a query sample']
blocks.content:
Record whether every run is slow or only some of them.

The higher a point sits, the longer that run took. A few points far above the rest are runs that took far longer than the usual ones. Performance might degrade during one stretch of time, and certain parameter values might cause a slow run. An average can hide those patterns.
blocks.tooltip: Each point is one run of the query.

blocks.content:
Open the **Wait events** tab.

If the tab is empty, skip the next steps.

blocks.tooltip: The breakdown names each wait event.

blocks.content:
Record the named wait event that contributes the most time, and its category.

The categories are **IO wait**, **Lock wait**, and **Network wait**. For example, `Lock:relation` is a **Lock wait** and `IO:DataFileRead` is an **IO wait**. The change is based on the dominant wait, and the fixes are grouped by category.
blocks.tooltip: Record the named wait event and its category.

blocks.content: You have a record of whether every run is slow or only some of them, and of the wait event that takes the most time.
